headlines: A Grown Child Learns to Ride, a Parent Lets Go
Bicycle Lesson Comes Several Decades Late
bodies: {A} helped adult child {B} learn to ride a bicycle on {street}. When the steadying hand finally lifted, both were surprised by how difficult it was to stop smiling.
A quiet stretch of {street} became a practice ground for {B}, with parent {A} holding the saddle. The lesson ended with an independent lap and applause from the sidewalk.
{B} completed a first solo bicycle ride after patient instruction from parent {A}. Neither considered the lesson too late, though both agreed on a shorter route home.

headlines: Bicycle Lesson Ends with Words, Not Wheels
Family Practice Ride Breaks Down over Teasing
Public Teasing Cuts a Cycling Lesson Short
bodies: {A} turned a bicycle lesson for adult child {B} into a series of jokes for onlookers. {B} wheeled the bicycle home and declined further instruction.
A cycling lesson on {street} ended when {B} objected to public teasing from parent {A}. The bicycle remained upright, but the conversation took a sharp turn.
{B} abandoned a first bicycle lesson after parent {A} invited passersby to laugh at each wobble. Witnesses offered more sympathy than the instructor had managed.

items.era_notes: Use an ordinary bicycle and a quiet street throughout. A is B's parent; neither role requires a particular sex.

headlines: Resident Pays for Shade a Town Must Wait For
New Saplings Give {town} a Long View
bodies: {A} paid for young shade trees along {street} and kept them watered through their first dry spell. The saplings are thriving, though the Gazette cannot yet recommend them for a picnic.
A row of saplings purchased by {A} has survived its first difficult season on {street}. Their care has earned public thanks and promises of help with the next round of watering.
{A} covered the cost of new trees on {street} and tended them until they took root. Neighbors praised a gift whose full shade will arrive years after the bill.

headlines: Late Frost Claims a Row of Young Trees
Sapling Project Ends in Bare Stakes
Tree Donor Faces a Second Planting Bill
bodies: A late frost killed the young trees {A} had purchased for {street}. The donor paid for replacements, earning sympathy even as the planting budget more than doubled.
New saplings along {street} failed after a hard frost. {A} covered a second planting and asked that the dead trees be cleared before anyone held a dedication.
{A} paid to replace a row of frost-killed saplings on {street}. Neighbors offered thanks, though the new trees will need another season before anyone can call the project secure.

items.era_notes: Keep costs as relative losses; use generic locally suitable shade trees without assuming a climate zone.

items.text: They say {A} has been taking credit for the crossword answers supplied by {B}.
variants: I hope {A} remembers to thank {B} for those crossword answers; a shared pleasure need not become a quarrel.
Apparently {B} supplies the words and {A} takes the bows.
Does {A} know all those long words, or only when {B} is sitting close enough to whisper?

items.text: I hear {A} has taught a dog to carry a basket but cannot persuade it to return the basket.
variants: They say {A} has the dog carrying a basket now; bringing it back may take another afternoon.
{A} supposedly trained half a fetching trick.
If {A} is such a good trainer, why does everyone say the dog gets custody of every basket?

items.text: Word is {A} and {B} settle arguments by writing complaints on paper and swapping them before speaking.
variants: I hear {A} and {B} read each other's complaints before arguing; taking a breath seems worth the paper.
They say {A} and {B} exchange written complaints first.
Do {A} and {B} keep those complaint slips, or is there a little bonfire after every disagreement?

items.text: People say {A} gave {B} deliberately wrong directions to keep a shortcut from getting busy.
variants: I hope {A} simply mixed up the directions for {B}; a quiet shortcut is no excuse to mislead someone.
They say {A} sent {B} the long way on purpose.
How many turns did {A} invent for {B} before that precious shortcut was safely out of the conversation?

items.text: They say {A} can pick a particular house out of a row while wearing a blindfold, just by the smell of its porch.
variants: I hear {A} knows a porch by its smell; old wood and familiar gardens do hold memories.
{A} supposedly recognizes one porch without looking.
Who checked that blindfold on {A}, and did anyone try switching the flowerpots first?
